findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "check_license" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Call before using any image, text, dataset, code, font or model you did not create. Checks one license (any SPDX id; curated readings for common ones, needs_rev…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "registry_lookup" appears informational but accepts parameters (history) that enable code/file/secret access.

evidence.snippet: query, history

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_license, check_rights_batch, get_pricing, issue_rights_receipt, check_listing · Private data: sign_up, get_status, issue_rights_receipt, gate_check, kya_lookup, kya_verify, kya_check, submit_feedback, check_listing · Public sink: sign_up, submit_feedback.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_license, check_rights_batch, get_pricing, issue_rights_receipt, check_listing · Private data: sign_up, get_status, issue_rights_receipt, gate_check, kya_lookup, kya_verify, kya_check, submit_feedback, check_listing · Public sink: sign_up, submit_feedback

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
